title: Release-policy translator: map canonical rollouts to Hosted / Dedicated / Private
creator: Anita Patel
description: Goal: Build a release-policy translator and enforcement layer that accepts a single canonical rollout spec (canary/A-B/shadow + auto-rollback rules + safety checks) and emits environment-specific execution plans for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The translator must preserve semantic parity (same guardrail behavior and observability signals) while honoring environment constraints: e.g., Private deployments may have no public control-plane egress, Dedicated pools sometimes disallow opaque traffic-splitting inside the GPU pool, and Hosted has full router capabilities and cost-aware routing. This ticket covers design, control-plane implementation, unit/integration tests, and an initial pilot rollout on an internal model. Deliverables: spec doc, control-plane implementation, integration tests against emulated Private environment, and dashboard updates for rollout visibility.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical rollout spec can be submitted via the API and is validated against schema
The translator emits an execution plan for Hosted that uses built-in traffic-split routing and progressive weights
The translator emits an execution plan for Dedicated that uses capacity-aware routing + explicit pool assignments when traffic-splitting is limited

The translator emits an execution plan for Private that produces a localizable plan requiring either sidecar-based routing or customer-managed DNS and flags features that need explicit opt-in (shadow traffic, egress to metrics)
Auto-rollback triggers (error-rate, latency SLO breach, quality-delta from evals) are mapped to environment-compatible actions (rollback, redirect to baseline model, scale-up) and executed end-to-end
Integration tests simulate a canary failure and validate automatic rollback happened and alerts fired in the console dashboard
Observability: rollout timeline + per-model metrics appear in Console with mapped keys for each environment
Security: translator respects KMS/HSM constraints and never encodes keys in control-plane requests for Private deployments
technical_notes: Canonical spec shape: deliberate minimal surface — phases: precheck -> canary -> ramp -> steady -> rollback-policy. Include signals: error_rate, p95_latency, cost_delta, eval_quality_delta
Translator will be implemented as a stateless service in control-plane (deployable in Hosted) with a pluggable executor interface for environment targets

Executor implementations: HostedExecutor (router api + streaming), DedicatedExecutor (pool pinning + capacity-aware splitter), PrivateExecutor (plan + customer-side agent hooks). PrivateExecutor must output an 'executive plan' JSON and a verification checklist rather than attempting to perform network calls into air-gapped clusters

Rollback window: default weight schedule 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with observability gate at each step and configurable timeout ; rollback condition default: 0.5% absolute increase in error_rate OR 20% relative p95 increase OR eval_quality_delta > threshold

Shadow traffic behavior: Hosted supports mirrored traffic to shadow model endpoints. In Dedicated, mirroring is only allowed if pool CPU slots available; Private requires explicit customer opt-in due to data residency/privacy and may require local sampling
Tests: harness will include an emulated Private control-plane environment (no outbound egress) using local mock agent and synthetic traces to validate plan delivery and in-cluster execution stubs
Permissions: rollout submission requires route-level or model-level RBAC; Private plans will include a 'customer-ack' flag for features that could leak PII (shadowing, external eval uploads)

risks_mitigation: Risk: Private customers may reject automated actions from control-plane. Mitigation: translator outputs a signed local plan that customer agent can opt-in to apply; default is advisory mode

Risk: Traffic-splitting on Dedicated could overload a pool. Mitigation: capacity-aware splitter refuses ramp step if projected QPS > pool headroom and instead schedules delayed ramp or routes to fallback model
Risk: Shadow traffic exposes PII when mirrored to external eval tools. Mitigation: require explicit customer opt-in and scrub sensitive fields; provide local-only eval runners for Private
Risk: Rollback false-positive due to metric noise. Mitigation: require multiple signals and use sliding-window aggregation + alert deduping before triggering auto-rollback
